children.text: Nara Smith is a lifestyle influencer who primarily posts cooking recipes from scratch and aligns her content with themes of life as a mother and wife. Joey Swoll is a fitness influencer who calls out bad gym etiquette in his reaction videos. Both Nara Smith and Joey Swoll use social norms in their content to generate engagement in different ways.

Nara Smith challenges social norms in her content, while Joey Swoll capitalizes on them. Social norms can be described as silently agreed-upon behaviors among the general public. Social norms can apply to many fields, including domestic norms, manners, etiquette, etc. People tend to react negatively when these social norms are broken, and these reactions can serve as a good source of content for influencers like Nara and Joey. Each of them garners attraction for their content with social norms and viewers’ reactions to breaking them in mind.

Nara's tendency to go against social norms and Joey's commentary that represents the voices of the people who follow social norms both drive engagement. In today’s social media landscape, profit from posts is driven by views, comments, and likes. Many creators will do anything they can to boost their engagement, including spreading false information or saying blatantly offensive statements. This practice has come to be known as ragebait.

Both Nara Smith and Joey Swoll use more tame forms of ragebait by either bending social norms or reacting to people breaking social norms to build their platforms. Although both of these methods may not be as bad as the extreme versions of ragebait, they can still be negatives in the content creation space.

Nara Smith is an influencer who portrays her lifestyle as a mother and wife primarily with videos of her cooking recipes from scratch. She has established her brand as one of living lavishly, eating/cooking cleanly, and loving her family through content that primarily consists of from-scratch cooking videos. In these videos, she is usually walking viewers through an elaborate recipe that she is making for her family. She makes it very clear through her narrations that her husband, Lucky, and her children are priorities in her life, and she takes pleasure in cooking up complicated dishes for them. She wears high-end designer clothes, speaks in a gentle, whispery tone, and displays a step-by-step sequence of her cooking process, and these elements come together to establish Nara’s familiar internet persona. Nara’s audience is most likely intended (at least on the surface) to be women and mothers who want to follow Nara’s recipes, aspire to live a similar lifestyle, or simply enjoy her recipes and/or brand. However, below the surface, it could be argued that Nara’s content is intentionally crafted to grab the attention of viewers who would be more likely to engage with content that negatively stirs them, otherwise known as ‘ragebait’. Many of her behaviors, such as the elaborate fashion, complicated recipes, and certain things that she says during narration, spark up engagement from annoyed viewers, which ultimately brings Nara more attention and uplifts her name as an influencer.

Joey Swoll is a creator in the fitness industry who mainly posts on TikTok and Youtube. He’s mainly known for calling out “poor gym etiquette.” He will frequently react to videos where someone is acting inappropriately in the gym and call them out. Alternatively, he will react to a video where someone is kind to others in the gym and will praise them. His creator brand is built around positivity. He even deemed himself the “CEO OF GYM POSITIVITY” in his TikTok bio. He has built a large platform from these videos with over 10 million followers across all platforms. With his platform, Joey promotes his low calorie sauces and one-on-one fitness coaching. He has become so synonymous with good gym behavior that users frequently tag him in videos to react to. Additionally, Joey tends to leverage ragebait content to his advantage. He presents videos that generate outrage and then takes the opposite position. This allows him to profit off of ragebait without actually creating ragebait.
